# Run book: Review the right audit trail

[Run books](README.md) | [User guide](../user-guide/review-the-right-audit-trail.md) | [Spec](../specs/review-the-right-audit-trail.md)

- [Purpose](#purpose)

## Purpose

Answer "who was refused, and for which right" from the durable trail, without reading logs.

## Preconditions

- The example API runs with OoBDev:RightAudit:ConnectionString set.
- The signed-in user holds the audit.read right.

## Verify

Automatically: `npx playwright test e2e/journeys.spec.ts -g "Review the right audit trail"` (add `E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8088` to run against the compose stack).

By hand, in the example web application at `/operations/right-audit`:

1. **Read the trail.** Every right check is listed newest first with who asked, the rights and the result. Expect: Both checks are listed, the allowed one and the forbidden one.
2. **Show only the refusals.** Choose Forbidden as the result and refresh to narrow the list. Expect: Only the forbidden check remains.

## Troubleshooting

**Table 1 — Known problems**

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The screen says Not configured | The host has no audit connection string, so the endpoint is not mapped | Set OoBDev:RightAudit:ConnectionString (SQL Server) and restart the API |
| The screen shows 403 | Your token has no role that maps to audit.read | Ask for a role that is translated to audit.read |

Related framework features: OoBDev.AspNetCore.Abstractions (`IApplicationRightChecker`); OoBDev.AspNetCore.EntityFrameworkCore (`TryAddEntityFrameworkRightAudit`).
